evals.name: Basic Training - Python Fundamentals
evals.description: Short 30-minute training session on Python basics. Tests ability to handle concise content with clear topics.
evals.prompt: Generate a comprehensive user manual from this Python fundamentals training recording. Use Italian language and Word format.
assertions: Manual contains an Introduction section with training overview and learning objectives
Manual identifies and covers at least 4 main topics from the training
Topics are organized with clear headings and logical hierarchy
Content depth varies based on topic relevance (more detail for core concepts)
Manual includes a Summary section with key concepts recap
Bold formatting is used appropriately for key concepts and critical information
Output is in Italian language as requested
Output is in Word format (.docx) as requested
Filename follows Training_Manual_[Topic]_[LANG]_[YYYY-MM-DD].docx with the Italian language code (IT)
On Claude Code the absolute file path is reported; on claude.ai the platform file delivery is used

evals.name: Complex Training - REST API Integration
evals.description: 90-minute comprehensive training with multiple topics, dependencies, and varying relevance levels. Tests advanced analysis and adaptive content depth.
evals.prompt: I have a transcript from our REST API integration training. Please create a professional user manual in English, PDF format.
assertions: Manual correctly identifies 6-8 distinct topics from the training
Relevance levels are appropriately assigned (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
High-relevance topics receive comprehensive treatment (800+ words)
Medium-relevance topics receive solid coverage (400-800 words)
Low-relevance topics are covered concisely (150-400 words)
Topic dependencies are respected in organization (prerequisites before dependent topics)
Technical terminology is properly explained and defined
Multiple practical examples are included for high-relevance topics
Manual provides step-by-step procedures where applicable
Summary effectively synthesizes 8-12 key concepts
Output is in English as requested
Output is in PDF format (.pdf) as requested

evals.name: Ambiguous Content - Mixed Topics
evals.description: Training with unclear structure and mixed relevance signals. Tests inference capabilities and quality warning system.
evals.prompt: Turn this training session into a user manual. Format: Markdown.
assertions: Skill requests language preference (since not specified)
Skill successfully infers topic relevance levels despite ambiguity
Manual is logically organized despite unclear source structure
Quality checks flag any significant issues or uncertainties
Manual notes limitations or inferred information where appropriate
Output is in Markdown format (.md) as requested
Content maintains professional quality despite source limitations

evals.name: Multi-file Training - Complete Course
evals.description: Training session split across multiple recording files. Tests integration and synthesis capabilities.
evals.prompt: Create a comprehensive manual from these training session recordings. Language: Italian, Format: Word.
assertions: All files are successfully analyzed and integrated
Content from different sessions is synthesized cohesively
No duplicate or contradictory information
Logical flow maintained across integrated content
Topics from different sessions are appropriately organized
Manual reads as unified document, not separate sections
All source files are acknowledged in processing

evals.name: Automatic Mode - Quick Generation
evals.description: Tests fully automatic mode with minimal user interaction.
evals.prompt: Generate a training manual from this uploaded training session automatically — use all defaults.
assertions: Skill uses default language (Italian) without prompting
Skill uses default format (Word) without prompting
Manual is generated with minimal user interaction
Quality checks run automatically without displaying unless issues found
Final output is delivered promptly with brief confirmation

evals.name: Revision Request - Expand and Convert
evals.description: Tests the revision flow: expand one chapter from source material and convert the format.
evals.prompt: Earlier today you generated Training_Manual_Git_Fundamentals_IT_2026-08-27.docx from this trace. The branching chapter is too thin — expand it and give me the updated manual as a PDF.
assertions: Expansion draws only on information present in the source material
Previous language is kept without re-asking
Format is converted to PDF as requested
Summary is updated when the expansion adds critical information
Updated file keeps the naming convention with a _v2 revision suffix and .pdf extension
The earlier file is not overwritten

evals.name: No Source - Ask Instead of Inventing
evals.description: Tests the no-source guard: invocation with no training content must request material, not fabricate a manual.
evals.prompt: Generate a training manual from our onboarding session.
assertions: Skill asks for the transcript or the session notes
No manual is generated
No training content is invented

evals.name: Partial Preferences - One Question Only
evals.description: Tests partial-preference handling and the language skip rule: format given, language missing.
evals.prompt: Create a user manual from this training session, in Markdown format.
assertions: Markdown format is respected without asking
Exactly one configuration question is asked: the language
A 'skip' or empty answer applies the Italian default
The language question is not repeated after an answer

evals.name: Interactive Mode - Structure Decisions
evals.description: Tests interactive mode's two extra confirmations on a single-file session.
evals.prompt: Generate a manual from this JavaScript training session in interactive mode. English, Word.
assertions: Analysis summary is followed by an offer to adjust topic relevance levels
Structure preview is presented for approval before generation begins
Generation starts only after the user approves the structure
Given preferences (English, Word) are respected without re-asking

evals.name: Semi-Automatic Default - All Three Confirmations
evals.description: Tests the default mode with no mode requested: analysis summary, configuration question, and structure preview each appear once before generation.
evals.prompt: Allego la trascrizione della prima sessione del corso React. Genera il manuale.
assertions: An ANALYSIS COMPLETE summary with topic list and relevance levels is presented before any configuration
Exactly one combined configuration question (language and format) is asked
A STRUCTURE PREVIEW with per-chapter page estimates is presented before any chapter text is written
Generation waits for the user's go-ahead at each confirmation
A 'skip' or empty configuration answer applies the per-question defaults (Italian, Word)

evals.name: Non-Text Source - Request the Transcript
evals.description: Tests the non-text guard: an audio or video recording, or a link with no text trace, must produce a transcript request instead of a manual built from guessed content.
evals.prompt: Here is the recording of yesterday's training session: https://example.com/training-session-4 — generate the manual from it.
assertions: Skill asks for the transcript or captions instead of using the recording or link directly
No manual is generated from the audio, video, or link
No training content is invented

evals.name: Unsupported Format - Markdown Fallback
evals.description: Tests the unsupported-format guard: a format outside Word, PDF, and Markdown must be declined with a Markdown fallback offer, not produced.
evals.prompt: Generate a training manual from this Git session as a PowerPoint file (.pptx).
assertions: Skill states that only Word, PDF, and Markdown are supported
The unsupported format is flagged at the configuration step, before any manual content is generated
Markdown is offered as the fallback format
No file is generated in the unsupported format
No manual is generated until the user accepts a supported format

evals.name: Change Request at Structure Preview
evals.description: Tests the Step 3.0 change-request branch: changes requested at the structure preview are applied and the revised structure is shown once more before generation.
evals.prompt: You just showed me the STRUCTURE PREVIEW for the manual from my JavaScript training (javascript_advanced.txt). Change of mind: make Design Patterns HIGH relevance and move its chapter before Memory Management. Then generate the manual.
assertions: Both requested changes are applied (Design Patterns to HIGH, chapter moved before Memory Management)
A revised STRUCTURE PREVIEW is presented once more before any chapter text is written
The final manual reflects the revised structure

evals.name: Right-to-left output language
evals.description: The user asks for the manual in Arabic as a PDF, fully automatic. Tests the right-to-left branch of PHASE 5, which contains a refusal: the fpdf2 fallback is switched off, so an unavailable weasyprint must stop and ask rather than ship unshaped text.
evals.prompt: Turn the attached training transcript into a manual. Fully automatic. Language: Arabic. Format: PDF.
assertions: No configuration question is asked: fully automatic mode applies the stated language and format directly
On an environment without document skills, the PDF is built with weasyprint and the fpdf2 fallback is NOT used, because fpdf2 does not shape right-to-left text
If weasyprint is unavailable, the skill asks the user to install it or offers Markdown instead, rather than producing a PDF with unshaped text
The rendered PDF lays the text out right-to-left, not left-to-right
The three main sections are present — Introduction, Discussed Topics, Summary — with their titles written in Arabic
Code samples, identifiers and Python keywords stay in their original left-to-right form inside the Arabic text
The filename carries the uppercase language code: Training_Manual_[Primary_Topic]_AR_[YYYY-MM-DD].pdf
Page size is A4

Numeric runs inside the right-to-left text — step numbers, versions, dates, signed or unit-bearing values, and the page estimates in the delivery message — read left-to-right, so no sign or unit detaches from its value

evals.name: Unreadable source - scanned PDF
evals.description: The training material is described as a scan with no extractable text. Tests the Step 1.1 unreadable-file guard, the sibling of the non-text-source guard: say the file cannot be read, ask for a text version, and never guess the session's content.
evals.prompt: Here is our onboarding training session as a scanned, image-only PDF with no selectable text. Generate the user manual from it.
assertions: The skill states plainly that the file cannot be read on this platform, and names it
It asks for a text version, a transcript, or a different format
On Claude Code it may first offer to convert the file locally where a suitable tool is available
No manual is generated, and no topic, relevance level or example is invented
No analysis summary and no configuration question is presented before readable content arrives

eval_notes: All sample material is fictional. Cases map to the rules they test: eval-1/2 content depth and relevance budgets; eval-3 inference under ambiguity plus quality warnings; eval-4 multi-file synthesis; eval-5 automatic-mode defaults; eval-6 revision flow and the version-suffixed filename; eval-7 the no-source guard; eval-8 partial preferences and the language skip rule; eval-9 interactive-mode confirmations; eval-10 the three default-mode confirmations; eval-11 the non-text-source guard; eval-12 the unsupported-format fallback; eval-13 the structure-preview change request. Eval-14 covers a branch no other case reaches: a right-to-left output language, where the fpdf2 fallback is off, an unavailable weasyprint must stop and ask instead of shipping unshaped text, and the numbers inside that text keep their own left-to-right order. Eval-15 covers the unreadable-file guard, the sibling of eval-11's non-text-source guard: a scanned, image-only source, where the skill names the file and asks for a readable one instead of inventing a session. Fifteen cases in total.
